summary: The TRIA Program Reauthorization Act of 2026 extends the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program through 2034. The bill modifies insurance loss thresholds required for certification, adds statutory requirements for the Department of the Treasury to issue public notices and final determinations on terrorism certifications within specified review periods, and updates related program reporting and technical dates.

affected_groups.effect: Covered by the seven-year extension of the federal terrorism risk insurance program and subject to a higher insurance loss threshold ($10,000,000) starting in 2029 for certification.
Subject to new statutory mandates regarding public notification timelines, formal review periods, final determination rules, and updated reporting requirements.
Receives formal public notice in the Federal Register when the government begins reviewing an act for terrorism certification and can view related annual reporting lists.

key_provisions: Extends the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program from December 31, 2027, through December 31, 2034.
Increases the property and casualty insurance loss threshold required for certification under the program from $5,000,000 to $10,000,000 for acts occurring in 2029 or later.
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to publish a notice in the Federal Register within 30 days of beginning a terrorism certification determination process.
Establishes a 90-day general review period for certification determinations, with an option to extend up to 365 days following the date of damage if there is insufficient information.
Requires the Secretary to issue an irrevocable final determination to the public before the review period expires if an act is certified as an act of terrorism.

Mandates that annual reports include a list of acts evaluated in the preceding calendar year along with their final determinations or concise explanations for why a final determination was not issued.
Updates various calendar year dates ranging from 2022 to 2036 for specific technical insurance calculations and changes program terminology references.
missing_information: The source text does not provide estimates of the financial impact or the number of policyholders affected by raising the loss threshold from $5,000,000 to $10,000,000.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The TRIA Program Reauthorization Act of 2026 extends the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program through 2034. The bill modifies insurance loss thresholds required for certification, adds statutory requirements for the Department of the Treasury to issue public notices and final determinations on terrorism certifications within specified review periods, and updates related program reporting and technical dates.
summary_detail.significance: The bill maintains a federal backstop for private property and casualty insurance related to terrorism risks through 2034 while adjusting administrative review procedures and raising program certification loss thresholds for future years.
